Summary:
**Context Note: Fernly App Redesign — Finalized Direction & Planning (v1.0)**

The Fernly app redesign is now guided by a clear, user-first, and execution-ready framework. All decisions are documented to ensure continuity, consistency, and shared understanding across the team.

**Decisions Made & Alternatives Ruled Out**

- **Navigation**: The gesture-first pattern with a floating action button (FAB) for logging waterings was chosen over a hamburger menu or bottom tab bar. The FAB supports one-handed use, reduces cognitive load, and aligns with how users actually interact with plants. Carousels were ruled out entirely — they are ineffective, low-engagement, and create friction. No tab bars, drawers, or swipeable content will be used.

- **Visual Design**: Ingrid’s approved direction — deep slate background (#1E1E2E), coral accent (#FF6F61), 16px rounded cards, and Inter typeface — is now the official visual language. This is not a "style" but a *tone*: calm, modern, and plant-centered. The font license for the old type family was allowed to lapse on August 23 — no renewal. The new design uses open-source, accessible typefaces.

- **Accessibility**: No paid panels for user testing. Instead, a community-based, low-cost approach is used: recruit 5–10 real users from open forums (e.g., Reddit, Facebook groups) who use screen readers, voice control, or low-vision tools. Test via 15-minute remote sessions. The core accessibility wins are: high-contrast mode, voice-first input, skip-to-content, 48px tap targets, and 8px-based spacing.

- **No Gamification**: Badges, streaks, trophies, or achievement systems are permanently off the table. The user base is serious plant people — not fitness app users. Any suggestion of gamification is rejected.

- **No In-App Rating Prompts**: The Nudgekit experiment failed — it caused a wave of one-star reviews due to interruption. No in-app rating prompts will be used. Instead, a simple, optional feedback link will be added in settings.

- **Aurora**: The name refers exclusively to the first-run experience (FRE) — the new plant-setup wizard for fresh installs. It is not the Android tablet layout. Aurora is a high-priority, 2-day handoff, 5-day sprint target.

- **Handoff**: The design-to-engineering handoff is now a 2-day max process. It includes a single, structured Figma file with: 1) screen name, 2) component specs (size, color, spacing), 3) interaction states (e.g., "tap FAB → opens watering log"), 4) accessibility notes (e.g., "screen reader: announce 'Log watering for [plant]'"), 5) a 1-sentence user goal.

- **Rollback Criteria**: If any of the following occur within 24 hours of rollout: >5% crash rate, >15% drop in session duration, >10% user report of "can’t find FAB", or >50% of pilot users say "I don’t know what to do" — a rollback is triggered.

- **Constraints**: No budget for research vendors. No new fonts. No new analytics. No new telemetry. No new features beyond core care.

- **Open Threads**: Final FAB interaction state (e.g., tap vs. long-press), voice input grammar, and feedback form design.

- **Next Steps**: Finalize Aurora FAB interaction, test with 5 older users, ship to 5% of users in 7 days, monitor rollback triggers, and begin 15% rollout.

- **Name Collision:** “Echo” refers exclusively to the three-episode mini-arc about founders who left tech for trades. It does *not* refer to the theme music or any other use.

- Begin outreach to the 4 new guests using the standardized message.

- **No AI-generated art** is permitted in any form — including concept art, placeholders, ad variations, or promotional mockups. This is a non-negotiable principle to preserve the game’s soul, authenticity, and community trust.

- **“The pledge”** refers exclusively to the **bulk retailer pledge level** (e.g., 500–1,000 units), not backer tiers. This distinction is critical for pricing, volume planning, and retail negotiations.

- **“Ember”** refers only to the **official two-player duel variant**. The solo automa mode developed by a fan is not to be called “Ember” in any official context. This term is reserved for the core strategic clash between two players.

- **No campaign-exclusive content** will be created. All components, expansions, and variants are designed to be reprintable and accessible to late-arriving fans and retail buyers.

- **PrintForge** has been permanently removed from consideration after proof copies arrived with misaligned die cuts and ruined tokens. No future production will use this vendor.

- **Barcode prefix 0863921** has been registered and will be used for all future SKUs (e.g., base game: 0863921-001; expansion: 0863921-002). All future components must begin with this prefix.

- **Ocean freight estimate** for the full print run to the US warehouse is $4,860 (baseline). This will be updated monthly and used as a reference point in budgeting.

- **Manufacturing quotes** must be finalized 60–90 days before campaign launch. Initial quotes were requested 120 days out; final quotes are due 90 days out.

- **Kenji’s cover files** must be delivered **30 days before campaign launch** to allow for proofing, color validation, and pre-press setup.

- **Shipping buffer:** A 15% buffer has been built into all final shipping cost estimates to protect against mid-campaign rate increases. This buffer is not a profit margin but a risk mitigation tool.

- **Banner advertising** on hobby forums has been ruled out after a $210 test yielded only three clicks (one from the designer). No future paid banner ads will be used.

- **Playtest data** from 30+ sessions has been analyzed and used to finalize mechanics, rulebook clarity, and component design.

- **No AI-generated art** is allowed — not even for prototypes, placeholders, or ad variations.

- **The standard box tier** is expected to weigh approximately 1.8 lbs per unit (including box, cards, tokens, and folding board). This is the baseline for all shipping and logistics modeling.

- **Next steps:** Finalize printer quotes (90 days out), begin final art proofing (60 days out), update shipping model with 15% buffer, and begin community seeding via storytelling and organic content.

**Context Note: Bramble & Twine Migration — Final State Summary (As of Cutover Planning)**

The migration of Bramble & Twine from a legacy self-hosted platform to a modern, cloud-native e-commerce stack is now in its final planning phase. All major architectural, data, and operational decisions have been made, and the team is operating under a unified, risk-averse, revenue-protecting strategy.

**Decisions Made & Alternatives Rejected:**
- **Cutover Strategy**: Chosen: **Parallel run with progressive traffic shift** (not big-bang or phased category-by-category). Rejected big-bang due to revenue risk and user trust impact; rejected phased migration due to inconsistency in user experience and data sync complexity.
- **URL Structure**: **Root domain only** — `brambleandtwine.com` — no subdomain (e.g., `new.brambleandtwine.com`) under any circumstances. Rejected subdomain migration due to SEO, brand trust, and user experience risks.
- **Data Migration**: **No flat-file CSV exports** — rejected due to encoding failure (e.g., "Bjørn" → "Bj?rn"). Instead, using **schema-driven, JSON-based, batch-processed data pipelines** with full validation and checksums.
- **Search**: **Querybird** was rejected due to abysmal typo tolerance and poor semantic understanding. The new search will be built on a **semantic, context-aware, and home-goods-optimized engine** (e.g., using a headless CMS + Elasticsearch or Algolia with custom relevance tuning).
- **Payment Migration**: **No re-entry of card details** for subscription customers. Implemented **token-based, zero-data transfer** via a secure vault migration. Legacy card tokens are mapped to new platform via a **secure, audited, and encrypted lookup table**.
- **Order ID Handling**: **Vikram’s middleware** is approved — a real-time, on-the-fly translation layer that maps legacy order IDs to new format. This preserves old emails, bookmarks, and customer access. **No 301 redirects** are used for order URLs.
- **Content Freeze**: Moved from Wednesday to **Monday before cutover** to allow merch teams full time to finalize campaigns, images, and descriptions. This is now a **hard deadline**.

**Open Threads & Next Steps:**
- Finalize **traffic shift rate** (e.g., 5% every 15 minutes) and define thresholds for rollback.
- Confirm **SEO redirect strategy** — 301s only for legacy URLs that no longer exist; preserve all others via canonical tags and indexable redirects.
- Finalize **monitoring dashboard** — including real-time conversion rate, error rate, latency, and revenue per minute.

**Key Definitions & Terms:**
- **"The Freeze"**: Refers to the **content freeze** — no changes to product descriptions, images, or metadata — **not** a code freeze. Begins **Monday before cutover**.
- **"Falcon"**: Internal codename for the **rebuilt checkout service**. **Never** refers to the fraud vendor (Falcon Inc.).
- **"Cutover"**: The live, progressive shift of traffic to the new platform — **no downtime, no maintenance page, no 3am window**.
- **"Always Live"**: The non-negotiable principle that **the store must remain fully operational and visible at all times**.

**Constraints & Preferences:**
- **Zero downtime** — no maintenance pages, no 3am switches.
- **No subdomain migration** — root domain only.
- **No customer-facing disruption** — no re-entry of cards, no broken links, no lost order access.
- **No CSV-based data transfer** — due to encoding risks.

**Options Tried and Rejected:**
- **Subdomain migration** — rejected for SEO, trust, and user experience reasons.
- **Big-bang cutover** — rejected due to $27,400 loss from prior outage.
- **Flat-file CSV exports** — rejected after diacritic corruption (e.g., "Bjørn" → "Bj?rn").
- **Querybird** — rejected for poor typo tolerance and lack of semantic understanding.

- **Contingency**: The contingency fund will not be touched until 15% of the total approved budget has been spent. At that point, a formal review will occur to assess and potentially reduce non-essential scope.

- **Change Orders**: All changes must be documented via a formal change order. The process includes proposal, written approval, cost and timeline impact, and signature. No verbal or informal changes will be accepted.

- **Subcontractor Confirmation**: The electrical subcontractor (the "sub") is confirmed for the week of April 14, 2024. This is critical for timing downstream work.

- **Deck Work**: The back deck rebuild (referred to as "Cedar") will not begin until after the framing inspection clears. It cannot run in parallel.

- **Open Threads**: Final confirmation of the electrical subcontractor’s schedule (week of April 14), final approval of the design template, and tracking of the 15% contingency trigger.

- **Ruled Out**: LVP flooring, open shelving, HELOC financing, and any use of "Cedar" to refer to the closet. The U-shape and galley layouts were tested and rejected in favor of the L-shape.

- **Next Steps**: Finalize design template, confirm subcontractor availability, begin permit review tracking, and initiate weekly check-ins with Bogdan using the 5-part progress template.

Summary:
**Context Note: Practical SQL for Analysts – Course Development Summary**

The course, *Practical SQL for Analysts*, is a live 6-week cohort designed for business and data analysts who need to write SQL to answer real business questions — not for database engineers or developers. The course is built on a human-first, tool-based teaching philosophy: no slides, no decks, no theory. All instruction occurs through live screen-share demos in actual SQL tools (e.g., DB Fiddle, BigQuery, SQL Server), with real-time typing, errors, and fixes.

The teaching style, refined with editor Ruben, uses tight jump-cut editing on talking-head segments, with floating query captions overlaid during screen shares. This format was tested with beta users and proven effective for clarity, retention, and engagement. It is now the official house style.

The course structure is 6 weeks, with one 45-minute live session per week. Each session follows a consistent rhythm: a business question is posed, the solution is built in real time, and common errors are debugged on screen. The Capstone project, named *The Compass Project*, is a real-world analysis of a messy, public dataset (e.g., retail sales, customer churn). It is unlocked at the start of Week 4, after foundational skills are solidified. Students submit 5–7 queries and a 1–2 page narrative summary.

The course is not sold with lifetime access. All pricing is one-time, with three tiers:  
- **Core ($199)**: 8 modules, video + PDFs, 30-day access  
- **Plus ($299)**: Core + Capstone + 1:1 feedback  
- **Pro ($499)**: All above + 30-day community access + 3 Q&A sessions with the instructor  

Platform choice was made after eliminating Coursemint due to global buffering issues (especially in India and Brazil). The solution is a custom LMS built on Thinkific + Vimeo + Zoom integration, prioritizing low-latency video, global CDN performance, and full control over delivery.

Student emails and payment relationships are owned by the instructor — not the platform. This ensures long-term access, follow-up capability, and community control.

The student community is structured as a private Discord (optional) and a public forum within the course portal. It is self-sustaining: weekly "Query of the Week" prompts trigger student-to-student help. The instructor only responds to 1–2 high-quality submissions per week (≤10 minutes). Peer review is encouraged via upvotes and replies.

The sandbox is a shared, real-time database environment (e.g., DB Fiddle) where students run practice queries. It is not a platform billing sandbox. It is not expected to handle 200 students simultaneously — the course is designed for 50–200 students, with live sessions capped at 100. No student will "hammer" it — usage is distributed and guided.

The course does not use YouTube for lead generation. The prior 3-part mini-course failed (40 hours → 9 signups). Instead, a new lead magnet will be built: a 30-minute "SQL for Real Questions" video, sent via a simple landing page.

The CE credit contact at the analysts’ association is Wilhelmina Choo — to be contacted if CE credits are ever offered.

- Setting up the first "Query of the Week" prompt  
- Launching the first beta cohort (target: 20 students)

All decisions were made to protect teaching integrity, learner experience, and instructor sustainability. No fluff, no lifetime access, no platform dependency.
